title: Flat K-flat lifts of resolved global Hom evaluations
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use a small representative of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $Q_X$ for localization and $\underline U_X$ for the termwise constant realization of an $A$-complex $U$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf, def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Tensor complexes use the direct-sum total convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $E$ be a bounded complex of flat module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Put $C=R\Gamma(X,R\mathcal Hom_A(E,K))\in D(A)$, with internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the constant/sections derived adjunction [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism].

There exists a K-injective representative $I$ of $K$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The global Hom complex $C_E=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(E,I)$, with differential $df=d_If-(-1)^{|f|}fd_E$ [def-pur-hom-complex], canonically represents $C$ as an object of $D(A)$. There exists a quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:U\to C_E$ with $U$ K-flat and termwise flat [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For every such $I,U,\alpha$, the formula
$$t:\underline U_X\otimes_A E\longrightarrow I,\qquad t(w\otimes e)=\alpha(w)(e)$$
defines a chain map. Its source is K-flat with flat terms, and its localization is the derived evaluation $\underline C_X\otimes_A^LE\to K$ obtained from the derived constant/sections counit and internal evaluation. There exist chain maps
$$\underline U_X\otimes_A E\xrightarrow{u}N\xrightarrow{c}I$$
with $N$ K-flat with flat terms, $c$ a quasi-isomorphism, and $cu$ chain homotopic to $t$. Under the canonical source and target identifications, $Q_X(c)Q_X(u)=Q_X(t)$. Moreover, for every scheme morphism $f:Z\to X$, exact constant-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] preserves the K-flat flat-term complexes $\underline U_X$, $E$, $\underline U_X\otimes_A E$ and $N$, and their ordinary pullbacks compute their derived pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 0G7D (lemma-factor-through-K-flat), with sections Hom complexes and Internal hom in the derived category; agent refinement for global evaluation, constant realization and flat sources, from old proof steps 1 and 3 of lem-pur-external-rhom-cone-pairing.

proof.text: Choose a K-injective representative using the native derived-category representation theorem. Convert the supplied bounded flat E to native flat terms, apply the native bounded-above flat criterion, and transport its K-flatness back to the required scalar coordinates.

Apply the A-linear evaluation-normalized global Hom model to E,I. This is the source result isolated in lem-pur-global-hom-evaluation-model; its conclusion is strictly the representative and normalization part of this item.

Resolve the ordinary A-linear cochain complex by the native flat-term K-flat resolution theorem. The existing constant-module flat and K-flat preservation theorems put this resolution in the coefficient point coordinates. Conversely, for every stipulated coefficient resolution, reflect those predicates back to the native module category.

The constant functor preserves flat objects and integer colimits, so it preserves flat-term K-flat complexes by the native functor theorem. Form its total tensor with E. The tensor lemma gives K-flatness and flat terms, and scalar comparison returns the exact predicates of this item.

Construct unsigned evaluation from the chain map into global cochains. For every map satisfying that pure-section formula, the defining property of the selected HomModel gives precisely IsResolvedGlobalEvaluation, by symmetry.

Apply the native flat-term K-flat target factorization to t. It returns N,v,c and their homotopy; scalar comparison verifies the required N predicate. Localization identifies homotopic maps and respects composition, giving Q(v) followed by Q(c)=Q(t).

For each of the four native flat-term K-flat complexes, upperStar preserves flat objects and integer colimits. Apply flat-term K-flat functor preservation and scalar comparison. Exactness of upperStar makes the left-derived comparison counit invertible. The four list cases finish the stated pullback assertion.
